description: Talk about named places from Living Server, rewritten: said in that place, and to a player who asks about it.

lines.text: East Svealand wolves keep adding, how do you pull them clean.
Jordheim is so big I still get lost on the way to my trainer.
Skona Ravine at 30 feels like the right speed.
The draugr in Cursed Tomb hit harder than they look.
Varulvhamn wolves are rough but the experience is worth it.
Jordheim smells like fish and smithing, just like home.
The Aegir zones look amazing, worth seeing even if you do not level there.
Salisbury Plains looks safe until it is not.
Campacorentin Forest at night is a bit creepy honestly.
Camelot is beautiful but I keep getting lost in it.
Avalon Marsh slimes, the experience that nobody admits to doing.
LFG Cornwall or wherever has room.
The moors in Cornwall are good experience if you can find a camp.
The barrows at night feel like a horror story.
Camelot at sunset is something else.
Lough Derg wolves are faster than they look.
Silvermine Mountains are rough at level 10.
Shannon Estuary crabs are free experience honestly.
Tir na Nog is pretty but my map skills are not.
Tir na Nog at night with the lights on, love this realm.
Jordheim is warm compared to the road outside.
Mularn is where every Mid learned to swing.
Vendo smells like wet fur, ask anyone.
Spindelhalla teaches respect for spiders.
Myrkwood in the dark is no joke, stay close.
Raumarik the cold bites through anything.
Nisses lair is where I learned to split pulls.
Svealand are long when you are new.
Malmohus makes me respect the north.
The Yggdra Forest feels old, like it remember the gods.
The Cursed Tomb is not cursed, it is just badly lit. Probably.
Odin's Gate has our pride, never let it fall.
The church in Camelot has an opinion on everything.
The guilds in Camelot argue more than they fight.
The Black Mountains are darker every time, or it is just me.
Avalon Marsh smells like old magic.
Salisbury is peaceful until the giants walk past.
Cotswold saw more of our first steps.
Camelot never sleeps, there is always a Bard talking.
The barrows give me chills, and I still go back.
Ludlow is quiet in a good day, enjoy it.
Dartmoor are wild, like something is watching.
The Forest Sauvage hides more things than any Bard admits.
The Tomb of Mithra is where I learned what fear feels like.
Snowdonia are cold than they look.
Tir na Nog is the kindest place in any realm.
Ardee is peaceful enough something notices you.
Muire Tomb taught me patience the hard way.
The Spraggon Den is loud, those spraggons never stop chattering.
The Coruscating Mine glitters nice until the miners down there notice you.
Lough Derg is the prettiest spot in the realm, prove me wrong.
The Cliffs of Moher make you feel small, in a good way.
The Bog of Cullen smells like old magic.
The Sheeroe Hills glitter at a distance, and nobody walks in alone.
The Cursed Forest earned its name honestly.
Shannon is calm enough, it is what under the water you worry about.
Emain Macha belongs to Hibernia, the Albs just visit.
Camelot is crowded and loud, but it is home.
Every time I walk into Camelot city I hear trumpets in my head.
Heh, the Cotswold road is where every Albion adventure starts.
Humberton always felt like the safest village in Albion.
I still think of Cotswold as home, no matter what level I get.
Caer Sidi is the hardest thing Albion has to offer, from what I hear.
Krondon is no place for a nervous healer.
Avalon City is the prettiest ruin in any realm.
Salisbury Plains go on forever, I swear the road gets longer each time.
The Black Mountains are Albion's way of telling you to slow down.
Llyn Barfog is lovely when nothing is trying to eat you.
Lyonesse is where good Albion groups go to grow up.
Campacorentin has the oldest trees in the realm, or it feels like it.
The Cornwall coast is lovely from a distance, up close it bites.
The Dales of Devwy are quieter than people say.
Caer Gothwaite is where the isles really start for us.
Avalon Marsh is the reason I own spare boots.
The bells in Camelot ring like they mean it.
The west downs feel like the real old Albion.
Caldey is a strange island, it feels like it is watching you.
The guilds in Camelot have been arguing since before I was born.
Ludlow has the best bread in the realm, ask anyone.
Dartmoor is the part of Albion the songs leave out.
The walls of Caer Witrin look tired, like they have stood too long.
Tomb of Mithra still gives me the chills.
Tepoks mine is where I learned to stop running into rooms.
Keltoi Fogou sounds friendly. It is not.
Dartmoor made me rethink my whole armor setup.
Krondon is too hot for anyone wearing plate.
The barrows taught me to respect a pull.
Caer Sidi at fifty still makes my hands sweat.
Stonehenge Barrows felt so big when I was young, now it is just home turf.
Hadrian's Wall has seen more Alb sweat than any field in the realm.
Every Alb remembers the first walk out past Hadrian's Wall.
The Pennine Mountains are beautiful if you never look over your shoulder.
Snowdonia is cold, steep and full of Hibs, sounds about right.
Forest Sauvage is where good scouts earn their names.
Hadrian's Wall holds more ghosts than any dungeon in Albion.
Castle Sauvage has seen more sieges than I have seen hot meals.
Snowdonia fortress is the first thing a young Alb sees before the real fighting.
Abermenai was the first place I ever saw an Albion army.
Abermenai taught me more about fighting than any trainer in Camelot.
Murdaigean and Caledonia, the two places that made me a soldier.
Darkness Falls is the best and worst thing in the frontier.
Darkness Falls is worth fighting for, the demons are a bonus.
After all these levels, a war horn in Jordheim still gets my blood up.
Jordheim smells like smoke and roasting meat, perfect.
Mularn is where every Mid starts and nobody forgets.
The walk from Mularn taught me to fear hill cats.
The Vale of Mularn is the prettiest place nobody remembers.
Haggerfel has the best smiths in the realm, or the loudest.
Svealand in the snow is the most Midgard thing there is.
Fort Atla always smells like wet wolves.
The Myrkwood trees are older than any Alb castle.
Vanern Swamp is the one place even Trolls do not like.
Raumarik is cold enough to make a Dwarf complain.
Skona Ravine echoes, every pull sounds like a war.
Malmohus is where Midgard keeps it is scariest things.
Gotar is quiet and that is why I love it.
Give me Myrkwood over any Alb meadow any day.
Aegirs landing looks like a whole new world.
The Gripklosa Mountains are where Midgard shows off.
Nyttheim feels like the end of the world.
Tuscaran Glacier is beautiful and it wants you dead.
Vasudheim feels like the edge of everything, in a good way.
Audliten has the best mead in the realm, no question.
The halls in Jordheim are so tall even Trolls look up.
Huginfel is a quiet town with too many stories.
Nisses lair taught every young Mid to fear little men in hats.
The Cursed Tomb is well named, trust me.
Vendo Caverns are a maze, every Mid has been lost in there once.
Muspelheim is too hot for a realm full of snow people.
Nisses lair taught me to respect a pull.
Spindelhalla is where Mids learn to love their healers.
Varulvhamn wolves are real Midgard monsters, none of that Alb ghost stuff.
Trollheim is the only place a Troll ever feels small.
Spindelhalla felt so big when I was young, now it is just home turf.
Odin's Gate is where every Mid learns what the frontier really means.
Jamtland is home ground and we fight like it.
Uppland is the first frontier view for a lot of young Mids.
Odin's Gate has heard more war cries than any hall in Jordheim.
Thidranki was the first place I ever saw a Midgard army.
Abermenai taught me more about fighting than any trainer in Jordheim.
Darkness Falls is the prize, the rest is just practice.
Darkness Falls is worth fighting for, the demons are a bonus for a Mid.
After all these levels, a harp in Tir na Nog still makes me stop and listen.
Tir na Nog is the most beautiful city in any realm, I will hear no argument.
Every time I walk into Tir na Nog the music hits me.
Mag Mell is where every hib's story starts.
Lough Derg shines like silver, best view in Hibernia.
The Cursed Forest earns its name every single day.
The Connacht hills always smell like rain and clover.
The Bog of Cullen is the only place in Hibernia I do not like.
The Silvermine Mountains are steep but the view is worth every step.
The Shannon Estuary is where I learned to swim, and to run.
The Cliffs of Moher make me want to sit down and write a poem.
The Sheeroe Hills are quieter than the rest, I like that.
Domnann looks like someone painted it with moonlight.
Worlds end is well named, I get chills every time.
Howth smells like salt and fresh bread.
Ardee always feels like a village from a story.
Give me Lough Derg over any Alb meadow any day.
Heh, the road from Mag Mell is where I fell in love with Hibernia.
Lough Gur is so calm you forget what lives in the water.
Ardee has the best bread in the realm, no question.
The fountains in Tir na Nog have heard every secret in Hibernia.
Cothrom Gorge looks like the land split open to show off.
The Vale of Balor feels like walking into an old curse.
Muire Tomb was my first real scare in this realm.
Spraggon Den taught me to hate small angry things.
Koalinth Caverns smell like fish and bad decisions.
Coruscating Mine is pretty until it eats your group.
Muire Tomb taught me to respect a pull.
Tur Suil is the hardest thing Hibernia has to offer, from what I hear.
Galladoria is beautiful and absolutely full of things that want me dead.
The Fomor are the oldest enemy Hibernia has, older than any Alb grudge.
Galladoria chews up careless groups and keeps the gear.
Breifine is where young Hibs learn the frontier is real.
Cruachan Gorge echoes with every fight it has ever seen.
Mount Collory is steep, cold and worth defending.
Abermenai was the first place I ever saw a Hibernian army.
Abermenai taught me more about fighting than any trainer in Tir na Nog.
Murdaigean is where I got my first real taste of the frontier.
Darkness Falls is the prize, the rest is only the road there.
Abermenai twinks in full crafted gear at 18, why.
Albs always turn up in Thidranki, let us hold the keep this time.
Mids are always last into Thidranki and win anyway.
Bards in Thidranki, nobody can catch us.
Murdaigean is where the twinks go when Thidranki gets old.
Just hit 25, goodbye Thidranki, hello Murdaigean.
Outleveled Thidranki, already miss it.
Dinged 25 and got kicked out of Thidranki, bittersweet.
Spindelhalla used to be the place to be, every night a full house.
Coruscating Mine was where everyone went back then.
The sunken Roman pillars in Avalon Marsh lead somewhere, mark me.
Isle of Glass is an old name for Glastonbury, and Glastonbury was always called Avalon. Just saying.
By the time we crossed the water, Avalon City was already rubble. Somebody got there first.
Avalon Marsh after dark feels like walking through someone else's dream.
Walked the shore of Avalon Isle and the same sunken pillars are there too. Same builders, I am sure of it.
Heard the barkeeps sold Avalon Isle iced tea before anyone could sail there. Explain that one.
Had a whole argument in Camelot about whether Avalon moved or we just never looked. Three hours, no winner.
A Bard in Camelot sings that the lady of the lake folded Avalon into the mist. Lovely tune.
A tailor in Camelot swears the old marsh stones are cut the same way as the walls in Avalon City.
I dare anyone to swim due west from Lyonesse until the map runs out.
Sir Arward took thirty knights into Dartmoor. All that came back was a scorched journal.
The journal fell out of the sky at Prydwen keep, they say. One word left on it: Golestandt.
A Roman lord and his whole household vanished in Dartmoor back in Uther's day. Nobody asked twice.
Those boulders in Dartmoor are not boulders. Granite giants, and they get up when you are not looking.
Never say the dragon's name inside Dartmoor. Old raid leaders swear she listens.
There is a corner of Dartmoor south of the ruins where the grass is all burnt. I turned back.
They say Moran the Mighty keeps watch in Dartmoor too. Never got close enough to check.
When the dragons first woke, the whole realm stood around in Dartmoor just to look.
Cardova holds a Roman emperor nobody can name. Cornwall is a strange place to bury an emperor.
Emperor Seleucus in Cardova has a name, so he cannot be the nameless one. The Forgotten Emperor is the real mystery.
I think the nameless emperor at Cardova is the one the dead Legion's march for. Nobody believes me.
Knock on the Cardova door twice before you go in. It is tradition and the dead seem to like it.
An old crafter I know swears the coins in Cardova have a blank face on them. Never saw one myself.
Merlin's barrow lies under Salisbury, right under the stones.
The barrows are the only place in Albion where the dead outrank the living.
There is a passage in the barrows that ends in a wall that sounds hollow. Never found the way past it.
Lady Nimue walks the Avalon Marsh after dark. The Wizards chasing their epic know her by sight.
Saw Lady Nimue in Camelot Hills once, just walking. She never looked at me.
Lady Nimue keeps the same road every day. Snowdonia by day, the marsh by night. Like she is looking for something.
There is a knight in green on the Sauvage road who will not fight you unless you start it.
The Green Knight waits near castle Sauvage like he is expecting someone. I bet it is not us.
Llyn Barfog has an Afanc in it. Arthur dragged one out of that very lake, so they say.
There is a hoof print stone up by Llyn Barfog. Some say Arthur's horse still haunts it.
Swam across Llyn Barfog once and something followed me. Never swam there again.
The monsters at Llyn Barfog gained epic status, they say. My experience did not notice.
A two-headed dragon called Xanxicar sleeps in the Crystal Cave under Avalon. Wait too long and the cave fills with lightning.
Heard the lightning timer in the Crystal Cave got longer. Still not long enough.
Caer Sidi sits on the road to Annwn. The souls in there are not meant to leave.
The old poem says Arthur sailed to Caer Sidi with three ships and only seven men came home. Bards still sing it.
Heard you never wear anything shiny into Caer Sidi. The dead go for the gilded first.
Caer Sidi is a prison of souls, and something at the bottom keeps the count. I do not want to meet it.
Krondon's ogres take orders from a warrior queen.
Heard Orylle keeps the deepest halls of Krondon. Never been that deep.
The orcs on Inishail fled the ogres, they say. Makes you wonder what Krondon did to them.
The Drakoran burned Avalon City to rubble, and someone held their leash.
The arawnites in Snowdonia pray to the same lord the Inconnu serve. Explain that one.
Dura'ek the Empowered leads the Drakoran in Avalon City, they say. Empowered by whom is the question.
Merlin's staff sits at Castle Myrddin in Snowdonia. Funny how Merlin never came back for it.
Mithra's tomb was every squire's first dungeon, and the promise room was where we all broke our promises.
Mithra was a soldier's god. Makes sense the tomb is full of soldiers who never left.
Overseer Tepok runs his mine like a guild leader. Goblins have bosses too.
Lyonesse was a drowned land. On a still night you can hear bells under the water.
The coast of Cornwall hides caves you can only reach from the water. Found two so far.
The Pixie Queen in Campacorentin holds court somewhere off the paths. I followed the giggling once.
Granddaddy Longlegs is a real name in Campacorentin and I refuse to explain further.
There is a White Horse walking Salisbury. Old folks say it is the one carved into the hills.
Cynewulf the Ghostwalker is not a Briton name. Someone else's war ended in Salisbury.
They found Inishail just off the coast and you can swim there. Makes you wonder how many more islands are hiding out there.
The Spirit of Lord Emthoro still holds Inishail. Nobody knows who he was.
Cailleach Uragaig walks Lyonesse. The old folk in Cornwall will not say the name.
Hadrian's Wall was built to keep something out. Nobody agrees what.
The Eye of Arawn in Snowdonia watches the whole frontier, they say. I wave when I pass.
The Bards in Camelot cannot agree whether Lyonesse sank in one night or over a hundred years. I side with one night.
Sir Arward took thirty knights into Dartmoor, and all that came back was a scorched journal that fell out of the sky.
Those boulders in Dartmoor are granite giants, and watch where you sit.
The shade of Uther walks the barrows still, guarding something older than the King's Wight.
The Green Knight on the Sauvage road never swings first. The trick is the second blow.
Arthur dragged an Afanc out of Llyn Barfog once, and the Legendary Afanc never forgave us for it.
Caer Sidi sits on the road to Annwn, and the dead walk in and do not walk out.
Krondon answer to a warrior queen, heard she never loses a fight.
The Drakoran burned Avalon City before we got there.
The old maps mark a ruin in the Black Mountains that nobody has found. Still looking.
Gossip in Camelot says someone saw lights in the marsh again. Nobody has found it since.
An Albion smith will swear that steel quenched in Llyn Barfog never rusts.
A pass came out of the Bog of Cullen's mist one day and nobody had ever seen it before. That is how Sheeroe began.
The rangers who found the Sheeroe pass swore it had not been there the week before.
Sheeroe is an Otherworld kingdom and Cuuldurach is its king. We are the guests up there, not the other way round.
The azure are Firbolg kin who pray to the sky, and they want every glimmer in Sheeroe burned out.
Never count the glimmers out loud in Sheeroe. My old guild swore it draws the prince down on you.
I like to sit on the Sheeroe ridge and watch the glimmers drift. You can almost see the Otherworld behind them.
There is a fold in the Bog of Cullen where the mist never lifts. I keep thinking another pass will open there one day.
The mist in the Bog of Cullen moves against the wind. I have watched it. It is looking for something.
There are tunnels under Breifine full of undead. Somebody carved them, and nobody is saying who.
Leave a bit of bread on the stones in Breifine before a raid. My guild never skips it.
The faerie court is said to walk the Cursed Forest. I have seen lights there that were not wisps.
Everyone knows the Cursed Forest for the werewolf camps, but the deep woods hold older things.
Luriquay walks the Cursed Forest and he is not as easy as he looks.
Dare for the brave: stand still in the Cursed Forest when something calls your name. I did it once.
Old crafter belief: anything you loot in the Cursed Forest carries a curse until it has been sold twice.
The old lord of the Muire house went mad and killed his whole household. It has not been quiet since.
Muire Tomb feels sad more than scary. A whole family laid down there because of what their lord did.
The Muire Hero still guards his kin down there. Loyal even now, I suppose.
Muire Tomb is decent experience that nobody wants, too gloomy for most. Suits me fine.
They say Tir na Nog was the Tuatha's refuge when the world turned on them. Now it is full of merchants.
Three of our towns carry Otherworld names. Mag Mell, tir na mbeo, Tir na Nog. I do not think that is chance.
The Tuatha came in on a cloud of mist, the old songs say. Maybe that is the Bog of Cullen's mist.
The Overseer of the Silver Hand in Coruscating Mine. Silver hand, like Nuada. That is no accident.
The Amadan Dubh in Connacht, the dark fool. One touch and you are never right again, or so the old folk say.
The Grey Man walks the Cliffs of Moher in the fog. Sailors say he is the fog.
Badb nests in the Bog of Cullen, a crow of war. The old folk say she smells battles coming.
Coruscating Mine was not open when Hibernia was young, the veterans say. Makes you wonder what else is shut.
There is a door under a hill somewhere in Hibernia that opens into the Otherworld. Sheeroe proves the doors are real.
If the Fianna wake I want to be there. Imagine Fionn's men at Emain Macha Macha against the Norse.
The Melancholic Fairy Queen sits by Lough Gur. I think she is locked out of her own door.
There is a story that a rider sleeps under Lough Gur and comes out once every seven years.
Bri Leith was a fairy hill before it was a valley. I think the door is there.
I have walked every hill in bri Leith knocking on stones. Still nothing. I will keep knocking.
I asked every Bard in Tir na Nog about the sleeping Fianna. Each one put the hill somewhere else in Connacht.
There is a hill in Connacht where the wind goes quiet. Stood on it once and felt someone waiting below.
Rode the whole Connacht coast with a lantern looking for a door in the hills. Found a lot of spiders instead.
Stood in a fairy ring in Lough Derg for a full minute. Nothing happened. Maybe it was the wrong night.
I mark every cave I find on my map in ink. Connacht has more holes in it than the map admits.
Heard a guild found an old door in a Connacht hillside. Nobody will say where. Probably nothing.
Gossip says someone blew a horn in Connacht and the hill answered. I do not believe a word.
Swam west off the Cliffs of Moher until the shore was gone. The sea just keeps going, and so does the fog.
World's End is a real zone. I went to see if the world actually ends there. It nearly does.
Climbed the highest rock on Vigilant Rock just to see the sea. Fog and more fog, and something big moving under it.
Allta Fearann turned up out of nowhere. One more place nobody knew about. The map keeps growing.
I swear there is a cave mouth on the Shannon side nobody talks about. Went twenty steps in and turned back.
Someone should swim out past World's End and see what is there. I will if two more come.
Dare: run straight through the glimmer camps in Sheeroe without stopping. First one to the far ridge wins.
Galladoria is where the roots lead. Hurionthex changes shape in there, so trust nothing that looks friendly.
The mantids kept Allta Fearann secret for generations. Their untamed land, they call it.
Heard Curengkur stalks Allta Fearann and the mantids only say the name in a whisper.
Balor of the evil eye holds Tur Suil. Never meet his eye, if half the stories are true.
I think the Fomorians were here before anyone. Balor's eye has seen every age of Hibernia.
Myrddraxis is a hydra at the bottom of Fomor, and they say the heads heal each other.
Balor's eye opened once and a whole valley burned, the Sylvan say. That is why the Vale of Balor looks like that.
Elro the Ancient waits out at World's End. I believe the name.
Glimmer dust from Sheeroe is supposed to make a dye that glows. My vendor did not agree.
I remember when Sheeroe first opened. Half the realm ran up the pass just to look at the glimmers.
My first night in Tir na Nog I got lost for an hour. The city felt like it went on forever.
I still remember the first time the Cursed Forest werewolves trained my group. Never went back without a Bard.
Someone in Ardee swears the Melancholic Fairy Queen smiled at her. I do not buy it.
Sheeroe is good experience if you can stand the glow. The azure camps never run dry.
Lore is nice and all but I go to Sheeroe for experience, not for the Otherworld.
My gran swore there is a door under a hill somewhere in Connacht, and it only opens when the mist is low.
On a clear day, from the Cliffs of Moher you can see an island that is not on any map. I swear it.
Tir na Nog was the refuge of the Tuatha, or so the Bards say.
Lough Derg are calm, but my fisherman friend says something moves under them sometimes.
The Melancholic Fairy Queen at Lough Gur weeps for something she lost. Nobody knows what.
Bri Leith is an old sidhe mound, so mind your manners there.
The cauldron sits at Mount Collory, and the Albs dream of stealing it.
Lugs spear hums before a storm, say the guards at Cruachan.
The eye of Balor at Tur Suil sees everything, or so the Sylvan say.
Galladoria, Hurionthex wears whatever face it likes. Trust nothing down there.
The mantids kept Allta Fearann secret for ages, makes you wonder what else they are hiding.
I keep a list of caves in Connacht nobody talks about.
Back when Sheeroe was not there, we thought the hills hid a dragon. Turns out we were right.
Gossip in Tir na Nog is someone found a door in a hill last week. Nobody has found it since.
They call it Odin's Gate. I have walked every hill of it and never found a gate.
An old map in our guild house shows a waterfall in Gripklosa. I have never found it.
The old Skalds say there is a sealed hall of the first gods under the ice, older than Jordheim.
An old Dwarf in Jordheim told me the Troll fathers built their first city under the ice, long before Trollheim.
Yggdra Forest is named for the world tree. Then where is the tree. I have looked.
Aegir was a sailors' story too, once. Then we all went there. Think about that.
Climbed as high as you can go in Gripklosa once. Nothing up there but wind, and a feeling somebody carved those ledges.
The mountains around Jordheim look carved if you stare long enough. The Dwarves say the gods did it.
I could swear there is a door in Jordheim nobody uses. I have knocked. Nothing.
Spindelhalla, Trollheim, the Iarnwood lair, the glacier. Every one of them was a rumour first. So what is the next one.
Odin hung on the tree nine nights for the runes. I think the tree is still out there, roots down under Yggdra.
Found a rune carved on a rock in Myrkwood that no Runemaster could read. Never found it again.
The sea past Aegirhamn goes black after a while. I turned back. Not proud.
Swam the length of Munin Sound once just to see where it ends. Cramps stopped me before the map did.
Modernagrav was not on any map I owned a while back. Now there is a whole island. What is next.
Back when I was new, we thought Malmohus was the edge of the world. Funny now.
Gossip in Jordheim is a hunter found a passage behind a waterfall in Gripklosa. Nobody can find it twice.
Heard a Troll in Jordheim say his grandfather walked the first city under the ice. Then he changed the subject.
The svartalfar spy on Malmohus from the edges. Whatever they are waiting for, it is not good.
Never say the dragon's name inside Malmohus. It is bad luck, my healer insists.
Malmohus is little known and less explored, said the old scouts. Still true if you ask me.
I think the dragon under Tuscaran was Gjalpinulva's mother. Cannot prove it, just how it feels.
Somewhere Fenris is still chained. His daughter sits in Malmohus, so lets hope the chain holds.
I remember watching our realm's first dragon raid form up outside Jordheim. Most of us never even reached Malmohus.
My old group used to bet on where people would land when the Glacier Giant threw them. Best was near Uppland.
Sometimes the sky over Jordheim turns green. The old ones say the gods are arguing.
The fire giants in Muspelheim are getting ready for Ragnarok. That is what my Dwarf healer says, anyway.
Fire giants in Muspelheim, jotuns in Vanern, frost giants on the glacier. Midgard is built on giants' quarrels.
The Shade of Gunnar walks Muspelheim. Nobody I know knows who Gunnar was.
The clay jotuns in Vanern were made by someone. Clay does not walk on its own.
One jotun outcast in Vanern stared at me like he wanted to say something. Then he swung.
I heard the jotuns of Vanern still pray to Ymir, quietly.
Rottild the Traitor lives out in Vanern. Nobody remembers who she betrayed.
The arachites keep svartalf slaves in Spindelhalla to tend the spiders. Grim stuff.
The arachite prelates in Spindelhalla pray to something in the deep. Never stayed to find out what.
Old scouts say Spindelhalla goes deeper than the maps. The webs hide another stair.
King Hresvelgr rules the werewolves of Varulvhamn. Hresvelgr was a giant eagle in the old songs. Nobody knows why a wolf took the name.
Do not whistle in Vendo Caverns. Something hears, my old group swore.
The Dread Lichess in the Cursed Tomb was a queen once, they say. Nobody says whose.
Nisse was a house spirit gone bad, my gran said. Leave out porridge and he is harmless.
I tap my shield three times before going into Trollheim. Laugh all you want, I keep coming back.
Heard Nosdoden was a proper dragon once, before Trollheim twisted him.
There is a bartender in Trollheim. His name is Olen. I have never been served.
Trollheim has an up leader and a down leader, Uppat and Nedat. My Troll friend swears it meant something holy once.
A Troll told me Trollheim still smells of his grandfather. I did not ask further.
First time in Trollheim we wandered for an hour. The halls just keep going down.
Our raid reached the mouth of Tuscaran Glacier once and turned back. The cold alone was enough.
Rumour says the jailer in Tuscaran Glacier holds one of the Troll fathers. Probably a story.
Someday I am climbing to the top of Tuscaran Glacier just to see what Queen Kula sees from up there.
Iarnvidiur breeds two-headed wolves in the Iarnwood. Two heads, twice the bite, same bad temper.
Two of the wolves in Iarnvidiur's Lair are called Hati and Skoll. The old songs say they chase the sun and the moon.
I heard Iarnvidiur is kin to the Fenris line. Every bad wolf in Midgard goes back to one den.
The crazed Morvalt believe that when the mother wakes, Trollheim will not be the only thing that falls.
Mortufoghus on Modernagrav might be part of the mother, some say. I want proof.
The Forgemaster in Delling Crater knows a recipe from before the gods, so the Dwarves say. He will not share.
My tailor friend swears the finest thread in Midgard comes from Spindelhalla. Nobody I know has any to sell.
The drakulv camps in Malmohus give decent experience, but every pull feels like the dragon is watching.
I skip the Iarnwood until 50. Two-headed wolves are twice the biting for no extra experience.
Raumarik is good experience but the revenant walks there. Watch your back.
The werewolves of Skona will not set foot in Malmohus. Ask yourself why.
Fire giants in Muspelheim, jotuns in Vanern. Midgard is built on giants' bones.
The arachites in Spindelhalla keep svartalf slaves to farm their spiders, and mind the webs.
The Morvalt dig on Modernagrav for the mother. If she wakes, Trollheim will not be the only thing that falls.
I keep walking Odin's Gate for a door nobody has found.
The old maps mark a waterfall in Gripklosa that nobody has found. Still looking.
Gossip in Jordheim says someone saw lights behind a waterfall again. Nobody has found it since.
The dukes in Darkness Falls are where most raids find out how big the gap is.
Gatekeeper Dommel has not left that door since Darkness Falls opened, or so the story goes.
Mutilator Xagalith has the most honest title in the whole of Darkness Falls.
Back when Darkness Falls first opened nobody knew what a duke was. We learned on our corpses.
Nobody I know has seen every room in Darkness Falls, and I know some very stubborn people.
The imps in Darkness Falls rob the bigger demons and trade the loot for seals. Little thieves with a proper trade.
Whoever holds the most keeps opens Darkness Falls. Count the keeps before you pack.
Darkness Falls changes hands more often than the weather. Check before you ride out.
Darkness Falls was a story long before it was a dungeon. A few old timers swear they fought there in another life.
Some say Darkness Falls feeds on the realm war. The more keeps change hands, the deeper it runs.
Heard the deepest rooms of Darkness Falls lead to the Summoner's Hall, where all three realms come together.
Darkness Falls is decent experience while your realm holds it, and useless the rest of the week.
One day I will tag a duke in Darkness Falls alone, just to see what happens.
Domnann is beautiful but the monsters are mean.
Vale of Balor feels like the edge of the world.
Delling Crater is hot in every sense.
Faraheim at night, eerie but good experience.
Iarnwood Dwarves hit like they mean it.
Avalon Isle Drakoran camps are always busy.
Avalon City is the prettiest place in the realm, no contest.
Hadrian's Wall is always where the fight is.
The Pennine keeps keep changing hands.
Odin's Gate fights never end.
Emain Macha Macha is always on fire.
Breifine keeps changing hands every hour.
Mount Collory road is full of stealthers, careful.
The trainers in Jordheim are a maze, every time.
Camelot city is so big I still take the long way.
Cotswold to Camelot, the most walked road in Albion.
Tir na Nog, glowing and confusing as ever.
Mag Mell to Tir na Nog, every new hib's first adventure.
The trees in Tir na Nog make me sleepy in a good way.
The demons in Darkness Falls keep me humble.
Thidranki is the most fun I have had at 20.
Twinks in Thidranki again, they hit like trucks.
Murdaigean keeps changing hands, love it.
